tasks.short: Issue equipment to workers and collect returns

steps.what: Issue suitable equipment to workers and clarify its intended use
Collect equipment when work ends and inspect returned items

tasks.design: Retain physical equipment issue, return and condition checks. Existing equipment guidance in {DOCS} supports appropriate use; the task does not establish a separate sign-out transcription baseline.
tasks.previous_blocker: Equipment must actually reach workers and be recovered in usable condition.
tasks.enabler_now: A record system does not remove physical handover or return inspection.
tasks.still_hard: Missing, damaged or unsuitable items need direct attention.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor checks the equipment at handoff and responds to condition concerns.
tasks.altitude: Equipment handoff responsibility and time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Describe damage observed on returned equipment

evidence.claim: Keeping physical equipment issue and return human is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is supervisor equipment handling, not workers' use time or purchasing.
Between s1 and s2 workers complete their existing assigned work and bring equipment for return. No new reporting task, machine return flag or outside-labour saving is assumed.
Existing equipment guidance remains; no custom tracking tool is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no workflow change is introduced.
research_questions: Which returned-equipment concerns require repair or replacement before reissue?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. Physical issue and collection retain time; no guessed register-entry component.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Calculate and monitor maintenance or development budgets

steps.what: Select budget scope and capture costs, commitments and planned work assumptions
Calculate budget totals, remaining allowances and variances
Monitor budget differences and discuss changes or corrective action

tasks.design: Configure fixed budget formulas and a variance view in {SPREADSHEET}. The supervisor checks source amounts and assumptions, then interprets differences and discusses action; formulas do not decide whether maintenance should be deferred.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated arithmetic can be separate from selecting and explaining costs.
tasks.enabler_now: Native formulas and pivot tables can repeat an explicit calculation.
tasks.still_hard: Missing commitments, scope changes and uncertain estimates affect the real position.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor understands practical work needs and explains the consequences of budget choices.
tasks.altitude: Less arithmetic, with spending recommendations and operational judgement unchanged.

reach.task: Explain the assumptions behind a maintenance budget variance

evidence.claim: Fixed budget arithmetic with human interpretation is an E1 model-knowledge design; the digest provides no measured maintenance-budget case.

assumptions: Boundary is supervisor budget preparation and monitoring, not accounting entry or authority to spend.

In s1 the supervisor produces period, work category, source reference, amount, currency, actual versus commitment status, planned quantity/rate and inclusion rule. All 45 hours remain for capture and checking; missing or conflicting figures require manual reconciliation.

Existing finance staff and suppliers produce cost records and estimates through their current work, with no new curation transferred. Test native workbook or finance reporting first; existing automatic calculations earn no saving.
Allow four focal hours for formula and classification upkeep beyond routine review. No free structured discrepancy code is assumed.
unknowns: Completeness of commitments and cost records
research_questions: Does the configured view reconcile independently checked costs and expose missing commitments?

already_counted.description: Cost capture, assumption checking and budget interpretation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R75 gross25 minus4 upkeep =21 net. High assumes repeated manual calculations; low covers existing formulas or substantial manual source reconciliation. Monitoring judgement retains time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct or assist equipment adjustments and repairs

steps.what: Assess the equipment problem and agree repair scope with qualified personnel
Direct or assist adjustment or repair within the agreed competence boundaries

tasks.design: Retain direct repair coordination and physical assistance within the supervisor's competence. Equipment guidance in {DOCS} supports the work; no generated diagnosis or instruction controls a repair.
tasks.previous_blocker: Faults and intervention needs depend on actual equipment condition.
tasks.enabler_now: Document tools do not replace qualified diagnosis or physical assistance.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden damage and unclear symptoms can change the repair scope.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor recognises limits and obtains qualified maintenance support.
tasks.altitude: Repair-assistance responsibility and time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Give useful context for a recurring equipment fault

evidence.claim: Keeping equipment-repair assistance human is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is supervisor direction or assistance, not the entire maintenance team's labour.
No free structured fault diagnosis or automatic equipment action is assumed.
Existing guidance remains; no custom diagnostic tool is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no process changes.
research_questions: Which fault symptoms require qualified maintenance before further intervention?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. Physical assistance and contextual repair direction retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor operations and resolve method or compliance problems

steps.what: Monitor operations to identify work-method, safety and compliance problems
Solve operational problems and agree compliant work-method improvements with workers

tasks.design: Retain observation, problem solving and corrective instruction with the supervisor. Current requirements in {DOCS} support decisions; no automatic compliance verdict or worker-performance score is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Operational and compliance problems require local context and direct intervention.
tasks.enabler_now: Record systems do not establish equivalent on-site oversight.
tasks.still_hard: A workable improvement must satisfy safety, production and applicable requirements together.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor recognises unsafe work, clarifies ambiguity and follows through with the crew.
tasks.altitude: Operational oversight and corrective authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Explain a recurring operational concern for review

evidence.claim: Keeping contextual operations and compliance oversight human is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is general supervisor oversight and correction, excluding separate crop inspection, practical training and maintenance assistance. Assign identical observed actions once in roll-up.
No free structured violation code or automated worker judgement is assumed.
Existing approved requirements remain; no custom monitoring system is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no workflow changes. Applicable national rules and supervisor authority are customer facts.
research_questions: Which recurring operational concerns require specialist interpretation rather than local correction?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. Observation and corrective action retain all time; no administrative evidence-production baseline is invented.

reach: Escalate recurring work-method concerns to safety specialists
